chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rifa'ah and Hafs, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to the House of Allah barefoot. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him walk, and when he is tired, let him ride.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one vows to walk to the Kaaba but gets tired?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in fulfilling vows, prioritizing the completion of the act over rigid adherence to the method when physical limits are reached. It reflects the Shia juristic view that vows are binding but flexible, allowing for riding once fatigue impedes the ability to walk, thereby ensuring the vow is fulfilled without causing undue burden.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rafa’at, and Hafs who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who vowed that he walks to the House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> bare-footed. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him walk. So when he is tired, so let him ride’.
en.sarwar: 19. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Rif‘ah and Hafs who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who makes a vow and commitment to walk to the House of Allah barefoot.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He must walk and if he becomes tired, he can ride.’”
